title: Longhaul: Survival and Crafting Sound Effects
shortText: 103 survival SFX: tools at fresh, worn and failing, breaks, the campfire, gathering, crafting, meters. WAV + OGG.
html:
Survival sound effects where the tools wear out: fresh, worn, failing, broken

103 survival sound effects: an axe, a pickaxe, a hammer, a shovel and a knife at three conditions each plus the moment each breaks, the campfire from a struck flint to a bonfire, gathering, crafting and building, warnings for hunger, thirst and cold, and three places as stackable beds.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No credit required. No revenue limit, no unit cap, no second licence to buy later if your game does well. Use it in as many projects as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell the sounds themselves as sounds. The full plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy paste credit line if you want one.

Everything is synthesised from code. No recordings, no sample libraries, no third party clips, so there is no upstream licence behind this one and nobody can content ID claim these sounds against your project.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 18 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The axe at all three conditions and the moment it breaks, the whetstone that fixes it, the fire at its smallest and largest, the campfire's whole life, and the camp at night with both of its layers.

What is in it

  • Tool condition (38)
  • The campfire (17)
  • Gathering (17)
  • Crafting and building (18)
  • Meters (7)
  • Places (6)

Tools that wear out

Survival games wear every tool down, and most sound packs give you one chop. Here every tool action ships at fresh, worn and failing, two takes each, so the sound follows the durability bar: a worn edge strikes duller and throws less spark, a failing head has worked loose and knocks twice, and a blunt shovel or knife takes longer to do the same work. Then the break itself, per tool, and a whetstone and a re-lash for the repair. Every step was measured from the shipped files: 12 steps, 0 failing.

The campfire

A struck flint, kindling catching, embers, a campfire and a bonfire as seamless loops (each brighter than the last, so a growing fire cross-fades up), logs put on, embers stirred, a spit sizzling, a pot on the coals, and two ways out: doused, or left to sputter. The campfire also ships as a lifecycle (4 states, every loop flag read out of the file).

Gather, craft, survive

Berries picked, an herb pulled by the root, sticks and rocks picked up, fibre torn, earth dug by hand, logs dropped and stones stacked; rope lashed, wood whittled, hide stitched, logs placed, a wall raised, a craft that works and one that falls apart, a tent pitched and a bedroll unrolled. Hunger, thirst and cold each warn at low and critical, and a warm swell says it is restored; none of it is a tune. And three places, a forest by day, the camp at night and a cave shelter, each a bed and a detail layer of one length that stack (6 stacks re-summed from the shipped files).

Already own our other packs?

Where this pack fills a role one of 7 of our other packs already fills (a pick on rock, a shovel, an axe, a fire bed, a doused fire, rope pulled tight), the two were measured against each other from both packs' files: 20 shared roles, every one a different sound.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a manifest listing every file by slot.
  • 10 seamless loops with sample accurate loop points in the WAV and the OGG.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 1.62 dB.
  • pack_proof.json ships with the pack: 948 checks, 0 failed.
  • No footsteps, no weapons, no voices, no eating sounds, no animal calls and nothing musical.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds, not field recordings. The measurements above are signal measurements, not a claim that it sounds good. That is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Pithead, the working mine: picks by rock hardness, minecarts, the winch and cage, timber and cave-ins.
  • Sixgun, the frontier: six-shooters, horses, a wagon on the trail, a saloon and a campfire.
  • Squall, weather as layered, rampable systems: rain, thunderstorms, wind, a blizzard and a wildfire over your camp.
